label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, B, C, D where the asset was C, A, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Front and back views show the brief's valve wheel: a ring rim with four spokes meeting a central hub, and the outline matches the brief's words in every view (front, back, the four angled views). Side views show the rim as a thin band and the axle stub through the hub, with no part sticking out or missing.

M2.reason: Measured 32.4 across by 32.4 high against the brief's 32 across (sizeOff 0.011), within 15%. Depth is 14.2; the brief gives no depth, so it is not scored against anything.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies and the views show: the rim, four spokes meeting the hub (counted in front and back views), the hub with its hexagonal steel nut on both faces, the axle stub through the hub (visible in left, right and top views), and the red collar blocks where the rim meets the spokes. The brief names no part counts beyond the wheel itself, so nothing asked for is missing.

M4.reason: Red paint on the rim, spokes and hub, with steel showing where the paint is worn at the rim's inner and outer edges, as the brief asks. The steel reads as bare metal and the red as painted metal in the front and back views.

M5.reason: The worn-to-steel bands run along the rim (front, back, front-left and back-right views), and dark cracks and grime show on the red rim (top of front view, lower rim of back view). The hub's steel nut is crisp at this scale.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test. In lineup.png it sits beside Half-Life's own props at the same scale and reads as a Valve-style prop. It was picked as the non-Valve model once in four readings (caught at the 1-in-4 chance rate), not the two or more that would cap it at 1.

M7.reason: The wheel stands upright with its face toward the front view and its hub at the centre of the origin. The brief names no front, so this is judged on upright and standing, which holds in the front and left views.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. Triangles are 376: over the third quartile (156), which is the kit's warning, but under the most Valve spends on props of this kind and size (422), so it does not fail. Views show no open or inside-out faces: the rim, spokes, hub and axle ends are closed in the front, left, top and below views.
